```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 5, dpi = 120,
                      message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(definetti)
```

# Idea

A composition of $K$ non-negative components that sum to 1 (allele
frequencies of a population, or the ancestry fractions of an individual) lives
on a $(K-1)$-dimensional simplex. The de Finetti approach plots it in that
reduced space:

| $K$ | simplex | drawn as |
|----:|---------|----------|
| 2 | line segment | horizontal axis, points jittered vertically |
| 3 | triangle | equilateral triangle |
| 4 | tetrahedron | orthographic projection with depth cues; several views can be faceted |

A corner is the state in which one component equals 1; position is the
frequency-weighted mean of the corners. Everything is built on `ggplot2`, so the
result is an ordinary `ggplot` object.

```{r source, eval=FALSE}
library(definetti)
```

# Example data

Three simulated files ship in `inst/extdata/` (regenerate with
`data-raw/make.data.R`; see `data.summary.txt` there).

```{r data}
ext <- function(f) system.file("extdata", f, package = "definetti")
# K = 2: population, locus, p1, p2
f2 <- read.csv(ext("allele.freq_k2.csv"))
# K = 3: population, generation, AA, Aa, aa
g3 <- read.csv(ext("genotype.freq_k3.csv"))
# K = 4: individual, group, Q1..Q4
q4 <- read.csv(ext("individuals.ancestry_k4.csv"))
head(f2, 3); head(g3, 3); head(q4, 3)
```

Rows must sum to 1; otherwise the functions stop with an error (or rescale if
`normalize = TRUE`).

# Two components: a line

```{r k2, fig.height=3}
definetti_plot(f2, c("p1", "p2"), colour_by = "population",
               vertex_labels = c("Allele 1", "Allele 2"),
               axis_titles = c("Frequency: Allele 1", "Frequency: Allele 2"),
               point_alpha = 0.6)
```

Tick marks are every 0.1; labels appear only at 0, 0.5 and 1 (`label_at`,
`n_ticks`). The vertical spread is jitter only (`jitter_height`, `seed`).

# Three components: a triangle

Genotype frequencies from drift trajectories, joined in generation order, with
the Hardy-Weinberg curve (columns are homozygote 1, heterozygote, homozygote 2):

```{r k3-hw}
definetti_plot(g3, c("AA", "Aa", "aa"), colour_by = "population",
               connect_by = "population", show_hw = TRUE,
               vertex_labels = c("AA", "Aa", "aa"), point_size = 1.8,
               legend_title = "Population")
```

Individuals are the same call with different data. With `colour_component` the
third component is shown as colour and the geometry is the view looking down its
corner (here a line):

```{r k3-colour, fig.height=3.3}
definetti_plot(g3, c("AA", "Aa", "aa"), colour_component = "Aa",
               vertex_labels = c("AA", "Aa", "aa"), jitter_height = 0.03)
```

# Four components: a tetrahedron

```{r k4}
definetti_plot(q4, paste0("Q", 1:4), colour_by = "group", view = c(25, 20),
               vertex_labels = paste("Ancestry", 1:4), legend_position = "upper-left")
```

One projection hides points, so several views can be shown at once:

```{r k4-views, fig.width=8, fig.height=7.5}
definetti_plot(q4, paste0("Q", 1:4), colour_by = "group",
               view = list(c(25, 20), c(115, 20), c(0, 85), c(205, -20)),
               legend_position = "bottom")
```

Far points are faded and smaller (`depth_cue`, `depth_alpha_far`); dashed edges
are hidden behind the solid faces.

## Colour for the fourth component

Looking down the corner of one component gives a triangle, with that
component's frequency mapped to colour:

```{r k4-colour}
definetti_plot(q4, paste0("Q", 1:4), colour_component = "Q4",
               vertex_labels = paste("Ancestry", 1:4), legend_title = "Ancestry 4")
```

Points with a high value of the dropped component sit near the centre, because
its corner is placed at the centre of the triangle.

The colour scale follows human perception rather than RGB values. The default
is a viridis palette, which is uniform in perceived lightness (CIELAB); other
members are chosen with `colour_option` ("magma", "plasma", "cividis", ...,
"cividis" being suited to colour-vision deficiency). A two-colour ramp,
`colour_range = c("lightgoldenrod1", "navy")`, is interpolated in CIELAB
space, not RGB. Avoid a white low end: low values then disappear on a white
background. Any other ggplot scale can be passed as `colour_scale`.

```{r k4-colour2, fig.height=4.5}
definetti_plot(q4, paste0("Q", 1:4), colour_component = "Q4", colour_option = "magma",
               vertex_labels = paste("Ancestry", 1:4), legend_title = "Ancestry 4")
```

# Customising the appearance

Text, theme and labels are plain arguments. Sizes are in points.

```{r custom}
definetti_plot(q4, paste0("Q", 1:3), colour_by = "group", normalize = TRUE,
               title = "Rescaled to first three components",
               figure_number = 1,
               caption = "Each point is one individual; Q4 omitted and the rest
                          rescaled to sum to 1.",
               base_size = 14, base_family = "serif",
               vertex_label_face = "bold.italic", frame_colour = "grey30",
               point_size = 3, point_alpha = 0.7,
               palette = c(Alpha = "#1b9e77", Beta = "#d95f02", Gamma = "#7570b3",
                           Delta = "#e7298a", Admixed = "grey40"),
               legend_position = "upper-right")
```

Anything not covered is passed on to `theme()`, and the result can be modified
as any ggplot:

```{r custom2}
p <- definetti_plot(q4, paste0("Q", 1:3), colour_by = "group", normalize = TRUE,
                    legend_position = "none")
p + ggplot2::theme(plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "grey95"))
```

# Argument reference

| group | arguments |
|-------|-----------|
| data | `data`, `freq_cols`, `normalize`, `tol` |
| mappings | `colour_by`, `shape_by`, `label_by`, `connect_by`, `colour_component`, `colour_scale`, `colour_option`, `colour_range`, `palette` |
| text | `title`, `subtitle`, `caption`, `figure_number`, `caption_wrap`, `vertex_labels`, `axis_titles`, `legend_title`, `shape_title` |
| ticks and grid | `tick_labels`, `n_ticks`, `label_at`, `show_grid`, `grid_at`, `edge_ticks`, `grid_colour`, `grid_linetype`, `grid_linewidth` |
| tetrahedron | `view`, `depth_cue`, `depth_alpha_far` |
| points and paths | `point_size`, `point_alpha`, `point_colour`, `point_shape`, `path_colour`, `path_linewidth`, `path_arrow`, `label_size` |
| frame | `frame_colour`, `frame_linewidth`, `show_hw`, `hw_colour`, `hw_linetype` |
| fonts (pt) | `base_size`, `base_family`, `base_face`, `vertex_label_size`, `vertex_label_face`, `tick_label_size`, `axis_title_size`, `axis_title_face` |
| layout | `vertex_offset`, `tick_offset`, `axis_title_offset`, `margin`, `jitter_height`, `seed`, `legend_position` |
| theme | `theme_definetti()` arguments pass through `...` |

`theme_definetti()` can also be used on its own:
`ggplot2::ggplot(...) + theme_definetti(base_size = 14, legend_position = "none")`.
